hypothesis: A deterministic lazy local-repair rule that performs at most one EDCS edge flip per external graph update can preserve the EDCS endpoint inequalities and a 2/3 finite matching-ratio threshold on the declared small bipartite domain.
competing_hypotheses: The one-flip lazy rule preserves both EDCS inequalities and the 2/3 finite matching-ratio endpoint on the tested domain.
A deletion or mixed update sequence creates a minimal P1/P2 violation or a matching ratio below 2/3 before the lazy queue catches up.
The proposed rule is underspecified or the independent oracles disagree, so no scientific endpoint is valid.

object.graph_family: simple labeled bipartite graphs G=(L union R,E), L=R={0,...,k-1}, no parallel edges
object.enumerated_domain: all edge masks for k=1,2,3 (total vertex count <=6; 2^(k*k) graphs per k)
object.adversarial_domain: all distinct-edge deletion prefixes of length 1..6 from K_{3,3}, plus one deterministic greedy mixed-update trajectory of depth 6

edcs_parameters.matching_ratio_endpoint: For every tested state with mu(G)>0, mu(H)/mu(G) >= 2/3; this is a finite diagnostic threshold for the variant, not a restatement of the asymptotic theorem.

lazy_repair_algorithm.initial_state: G=empty, H=empty, dirty FIFO contains no vertices
external_update: Apply one insertion or deletion to G.
If an inserted edge is absent from H and is P2-deficient, enqueue both endpoints; if a deleted edge is in H, remove it and enqueue both endpoints; enqueue endpoints of every changed H edge.
Perform at most one repair flip per external update.
Scan dirty vertices FIFO; for the first dirty vertex, inspect all incident G edges in lexicographic order.
Choose the lexicographically smallest P1-violating used edge (remove it) before any P2-deficient unused edge (add it).
After a flip, enqueue both endpoints and retain the dirty vertex; if no incident violation exists, remove that vertex from the dirty FIFO.
Do not perform a global rebuild, orientation, bucket refresh, alternating-path search, or more than one H flip per external update.
lazy_repair_algorithm.determinism: No random choices; all edges and queue operations are lexicographically/FIFO ordered.
lazy_repair_algorithm.variant_scope: This is intentionally not the Bernstein-Stein dynamic maintenance algorithm.

oracles.runner_invariant_oracle: direct degree-sum scan over every G edge and H edge
oracles.independent_validator: separately implemented recursive right-vertex bitmask maximum matching and independent degree-sum replay

falsification_gate.failure: first state with any P1 violation, P2 violation, or exact mu(H)/mu(G) < 2/3; record update index, operation, H/G edges and all relevant endpoint degree sums
falsification_gate.success: no failure over all declared static masks, all K3,3 deletion prefixes, and the greedy mixed trajectory; report finite coverage and do not claim a proof
falsification_gate.invalid: implementation hash/oracle disagreement, incomplete trace, resource limit, or inability to define the deterministic rule
